title: Decide: entity-first vs triple-first semantics
description: Clarify whether hooray uses entity-first semantics (documents override previous versions — a new document for an entity replaces all prior attributes) or triple-first semantics (only previous versions of the same triple get overridden — existing attributes not mentioned in an update are preserved). This is a fundamental design decision that affects how writes/retractions work throughout the system.

title: Clarify openLevel semantics for iterators with non-zero first participating level
description:
## Problem

The join algorithm has an ambiguity around `openLevel` at level 0. If `openLevel` does not need to be called at the first level (level 0), then there is no way to differentiate between:

1. An iterator that is naturally at its first level (already ready to use)
2. An iterator that needs to be explicitly opened before use

This becomes a concrete problem with iterators whose first participating level is not 0 but at a later level (e.g., a `createSingleLevel` iterator at level 1, or an `AVLFnLeapfrogIndex` at `outputLevel`). When the join descends to those levels, some iterators at that level have already been opened (multi-level iterators that were opened progressively from level 0), while others haven't been opened at all (single-level iterators that only participate at that level).

## Concrete example

In a 3-level join with:
- `first` at level 0
- `second` at level 1 (single-level)
- `fnIndex` + `sums` at level 2

After exhausting `second` for `first=1`, the join backtracks to level 0 and advances `first` to 2. When it re-descends to level 1, `second` is still exhausted — `closeLevel` was never called on it (the close filter skips it), and `openLevel` is never called on it (it's not in `participants[0]`). The join has no mechanism to reset it.

## Current workaround

The join now calls `openLevel` on all participants at each level during descent (`participants[level + 1].map { it.openLevel() }`). This works but conflates "initialize for first use" with "reset for reuse", and may cause unnecessary open/close cycles on multi-level iterators.

## Resolution

Need to decide on clear semantics: should `openLevel` always be called before first use at every level? Should there be a separate reset mechanism? The `reinit` method exists but is a full reset, not a per-level reset.
